# Story 20.2: Wire --dms-* tokens into Tailwind theme.extend and delete dead utility classes

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story

As a developer,
I want the `--dms-*` token system wired into Tailwind's `theme.extend` so utilities and Material SCSS share one source, with dead custom utility classes in `styles.scss` deleted,
So that there is a single theming source of truth and no visual drift (P1 item #3 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Story 20.1's red-phase tests pass: `tailwind.config.js`'s `theme.extend` maps its theme values to the `--dms-*` custom properties, and no dead custom utility class remains in `styles.scss`.
2. Tailwind utilities and Material SCSS resolve from one shared token source — `theme.extend` references `var(--dms-*)` rather than duplicating hardcoded color/spacing values.
3. No visual drift occurs: the resolved values are unchanged (the current SCSS and Tailwind values already match, so wiring them to the same tokens produces identical output).
4. Dead custom utility classes in `apps/dms-material/src/styles.scss` are deleted — no orphaned class definitions remain.
5. The previously-skipped tests from Story 20.1 are unskipped (`.skip()` removed) and pass under `nx test dms-material`; the full dms-material suite is green with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1 (AC: #1–#4): Remove skip markers and confirm red.
  - [ ] 1.1 In the specs added by Story 20.1, remove every `it.skip` marker and run `nx test dms-material`, confirming the new assertions FAIL against current code (red).
- [ ] Task 2 (AC: #2): Wire `--dms-*` tokens into Tailwind `theme.extend`.
  - [ ] 2.1 In `apps/dms-material/tailwind.config.js`, update `theme.extend` so that color/spacing/font-size values reference the `--dms-*` custom properties (e.g., `'colors': { 'dms-primary': 'var(--dms-color-primary)' }`) rather than duplicating hardcoded hex/px values.
  - [ ] 2.2 Verify the resolved values are identical to before (no visual drift) — the current SCSS and Tailwind values already match, so this is a pure source-consolidation change.
- [ ] Task 3 (AC: #4): Delete dead custom utility classes from `styles.scss`.
  - [ ] 3.1 In `apps/dms-material/src/styles.scss`, identify and delete every custom utility class that is not referenced by any component or template.
  - [ ] 3.2 Confirm no remaining class definition in `styles.scss` is orphaned.
- [ ] Task 4 (AC: #5): Confirm green suite.
  - [ ] 4.1 Run `nx test dms-material` and confirm fully green with Story 20.1's tests now passing (unskipped).

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** the `--dms-*` tokens are currently defined in the theme SCSS but Tailwind's `theme.extend` does not consume them as its source — two parallel theming systems exist. Wiring Tailwind to the same tokens ends the drift, and deleting dead utility classes removes unused code (P1 item #3 from Aspect 9).
- **First task is always unskip → confirm red → implement.** The red-phase tests from Story 20.1 define the target; do not edit their assertions to make them pass, only the production code/config.
- **No visual drift:** the current SCSS and Tailwind values already match. This story consolidates the source — it does NOT change any resolved value. If a value differs between SCSS and Tailwind, resolve the discrepancy by keeping the SCSS value (the design-token source of truth) and updating Tailwind to reference it.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; dms-material tests run via `nx test dms-material`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/dms-material/tailwind.config.js` (`theme.extend` → reference `var(--dms-*)`).
- Modify: `apps/dms-material/src/styles.scss` (delete dead custom utility classes).
- Modify: Story 20.1's spec (remove `.skip()` markers only — no assertion changes).
